Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

In the part of Italy that is known as Umbria, there stands the little town of Assisi, built on the slopes of Monte Subasio. Assisi is a very old city - some say it dates as far back as 400 or 500 B.C. - and underneath its streets are long passages that come out far away in the hills, as if the citizens had used them in times of siege as a means of escape. If you studied its ruins of temples, theatres, and circuses, you would learn a great deal of history, not only of Assisi itself but of Rome as well. Totila, the Goth, halted there for a short time on his way to besiege the Eternal City. Charlemagne passed through it two hundred and fifty years later; while in the struggle for power between the pope and the emperor during the Middle Ages, the town sided first with one and then with the other. But, against one enemy, the people of Assisi never ceased fighting, and that was with the citizens of Perugia, which lay across the hills and could be seen plainly from the castle on the top. Among all the merchants of Assisi, none was so rich or well thought of as Bernadone, who carried on with France a large trade in silk and embroidered stuff. He had an only son, Giovanni, or John, born in 1182, and, as soon as the child was four or five years old, he had been taught French, so that by and by his father might send him across the sea to sell his goods to the noble ladies of the French court, and as no one in Assisi ever thought of learning any language but Italian, the boy was nicknamed "Il Francesco," or "the Frenchman." This nickname would become symbolic of a remarkable future. Giovanni would grow up to transform not only his own life but also the lives of countless others, embodying values of humility and compassion that continue to resonate around the world.

What was the likely purpose of the long passages underneath the streets of Assisi?
options_en: They were used for storing goods.
They functioned as aqueducts for water supply.
They were built as places of worship.
They provided a way to evade danger during sieges.
questions.solution_en: The passage states, 'Assisi is a very old city - some say it dates as far back as 400 or 500 B.C. - and underneath its streets are long passages that come out far away in the hills, as if the citizens had used them in times of siege as a means of escape.' This indicates that the passages were designed to help citizens escape or evade danger during times of siege, rather than for storage, aqueducts, or worship. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

You can always ____________ Michael in case of a crisis.
questions.solution_en:
The phrasal verb 'do over' means a new attempt or opportunity to do something after a previous attempt has been unsuccessful or unsatisfactory; 'count on' means rely on someone or something; 'drop off' means fall asleep easily, especially without intending to; 'get along' means have a harmonious or friendly relationship. According to the meanings mentioned above, option b) fits in the blank contextually and gives a meaningful sentence. Filling the blank with 'count on' gives the meaning that the subject 'you' can depend on Michael in case of crisis.

The correct sentence is: You can always count on Michael in case of a crisis.

Hence, b) is the correct answer.

Note: Phrasal verb: A phrase that consists of a verb with a preposition or adverb or both, the meaning of which is different from the meaning of its separate parts. Example: She has always looked down on me. Here, the phrasal verb 'to look down on someone' doesn't mean that you are looking down from a higher place at someone who is below you; it means that you think that you are better than someone.

questions.q_en:
Directions : Read the following passage and answer the questions given after it.

Wetlands are amongst the most productive ecosystems on the Earth and provide many important services to human society. They exhibit enormous diversity according to their genesis, geographical location, water regime and chemistry, dominant species, and soil and sediment characteristics. Globally, the areal extent of wetland ecosystems ranges from 917 million hectares (m ha) to more than 1275 m ha. One of the first widely used wetland classifications systems, devised by Cowardin et al., 1979, categorized wetlands into marine (coastal wetlands), estuarine (including deltas, tidal marshes, and mangrove swamps), lacustrine (lakes), riverine (along rivers and streams), and palustrine ( marshes, swamps and bogs) based on their hydrological, ecological and geological characteristics.

Ramsar Convention on Wetlands was an international treaty signed in 1971. Overall, 1052 sites in Europe; 289 sites in Asia; 359 sites in Africa; 175 sites in South America; 211 sites in North America; and 79 sites in Oceania region have been identified as Ramsar sites or wetlands of International importance.

As per the Ramsar Convention definition most of the natural water bodies (such as rivers, lakes, coastal lagoons, mangroves, peat land, coral reefs) and man- made wetlands (such as ponds, farm ponds, irrigated fields, sacred groves, salt pans, reservoirs, gravel pits, sewage farms and canals) in India constitute the wetland ecosystem distributed in different geographical regions ranging from Himalayas to Deccan plateau. As of February, 2022, India has 49 Ramsar sites covering an area of 10,93,636 hectares, the highest in South Asia.

As per the estimates, India has about 757.06 thousand wetlands with a total wetland area of 15.3 m ha, accounting for nearly 4.7% of the total geographical area of the country. Out of this, areas under inland wetlands accounts for 69%, coastal wetlands 27%, and other wetlands (smaller than 2.25 ha) 4%.

Gujarat has the highest proportion (17.5%) and Mizoram has the lowest proportion (0.66%) of the area under wetlands. Among Union Territories, Lakshadweep has the highest proportion (around 96%) and Chandigarh has the least proportion (3%) of geographical area under wetlands.

Under which category of wetlands, are delta and mangrove swamps included?
questions.solution_en:
Refer to the following sentence from the first paragraph - "One of the first widely used wetland classifications systems, devised by Cowardin et al., 1979, categorized wetlands into marine (coastal wetlands), estuarine (including deltas, tidal marshes, and mangrove swamps), lacustrine (lakes), riverine (along rivers and streams), and palustrine ( marshes, swamps and bogs) based on their hydrological, ecological and geological characteristics."

So, delta and mangrove swamps come under category of estuarine wetlands.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

If you tries to dictate your terms, I don't think we can work together.
questions.solution_en:
The pronoun 'you' is used with plural verb, and not the singular verb. So, singular verb 'tries' should be substituted.

The helping verb 'have' should be followed by the past participle (V3) form of verb, but 'try' is the base verb, so option (c) is incorrect.

'Were tried' is the construct for the sentence in passive voice, whereas the verb 'tried' is action done by the subject, and not on the subject. So, option (d) is incorrect as well.

'Try' is the plural verb which can follow the pronoun 'you'. So, option (a) can substitute the underlined segment.

The correct sentence is: If you try to dictate your terms, I don't think we can work together.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

options_en: Who taught you English grammar and composition?
Who had taught you English grammar and composition?
Whom taught you English grammar and composition?
Who has taught you English grammar and composition?
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb and the preposition "by" is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

In Active voice (look at the options), it should be in interrogative form. These are "wh" questions that don't take "yes" or "no" as an answer.

"By whom?" is changed into "Who" while transforming from Passive to Active.

For example:

By whom are you taught Math? (or) Who are you taught Math by? (Passive)

Who teaches you Math? (Active)

"Who" is changed into "Whom" while transforming from Passive to Active.

For example:

Who is being taught by you? (Passive)

Whom are you teaching? (Active)

The sentence in the Passive voice is in Past Indefinite. So, the sentence in the Active voice should be in Past Indefinite.

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): Who taught you English grammar and composition?

questions.q_en:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

(a) by automating complex tasks,

(b) from healthcare to finance,

(c) enhancing decision-making capabilities,

(d) artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming various industries,

(e) and creating innovative solutions for challenging problems
questions.solution_en:
(d) Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming various industries, - This forms the main clause of the sentence, introducing the subject (Artificial intelligence) and the primary verb (is rapidly transforming).

(b) from healthcare to finance, - This prepositional phrase provides examples of the "various industries" mentioned in (d), adding specificity. So far: "Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming various industries, from healthcare to finance,"

(a) by automating complex tasks, - This phrase, starting with "by," begins to explain how artificial intelligence is transforming these industries. It introduces the first method or impact. Now: "...from healthcare to finance, by automating complex tasks,"

(c) enhancing decision-making capabilities, - This participial phrase presents the second method/impact, parallel in structure to "automating complex tasks." It continues the explanation: "...by automating complex tasks, enhancing decision-making capabilities,"

(e) and creating innovative solutions for challenging problems - This phrase, beginning with "and," lists the third method/impact, completing the series of explanations for how AI transforms industries.

Alternately, acedb is also a possible arrangement.

Final sentence: "Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming various industries, from healthcare to finance, by automating complex tasks, enhancing decision-making capabilities, and creating innovative solutions for challenging problems."

"By automating complex tasks, enhancing decision-making capabilities, and creating innovative solutions for challenging problems, artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming various industries, from healthcare to finance."

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Unless you do not work diligently / towards your ambitious career goals, / achieving significant success will be quite difficult.
options_en: achieving significant success will be quite difficult
Unless you do not work diligently
questions.solution_en:
The error is in the part "Unless you do not work diligently". "Unless" is a subordinating conjunction that means "if...not" or "except if." It already implies a negative condition. Therefore, using another negative like "do not" after "unless" creates a double negative and makes the sentence illogical or redundant. The "do not" should be removed.

Correct Sentence: Unless you work diligently towards your ambitious career goals, achieving significant success will be quite difficult.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Note:

· Subordinating conjunctions: Subordinating conjunctions connect subordinate clauses (dependent clauses) to the main clause of a sentence. "Unless" is a subordinating conjunction.

· Redundancy/Double Negative: The use of "do not" with "unless" is redundant because "unless" inherently carries a negative meaning.

questions.q_en:
Substitute the underlined word-segment with most appropriate idiom.

When listening to the politician's promises, it's wise to regard them with some scepticism.
options_en: take them with a grain of salt
bite off more than one can chew
questions.solution_en:
The phrase "regard them with some scepticism" refers to not fully believing something or being doubtful about its truth or likelihood. The idiom "take something with a grain of salt" means to not completely believe something that you are told because you think it is unlikely to be true or accurate. Here, "them" (implied "it" in the base idiom "take it with a grain of salt") refers to the promises. This fits the context of being cautious about a politician's promises. Therefore, it is the most suitable idiomatic replacement.

a) go the extra mile - to make a special effort. (Unrelated to skepticism.)

b) cry over spilt milk - to be unhappy about what cannot be undone. (Unrelated to believing promises.)

d) bite off more than one can chew - to take on a task that is too big or difficult. (Unrelated to scepticism about statements.)

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. So when XY Corp talked about the communication interruption device, it immediately escalated tensions between two major powerful countries.

B. Nearly every country in the world uses hackers to gather intelligence.

C. Major powers like the United States and Russia have large stables of such groups - many of which have been given colourful nicknames by cybersecurity experts.

D. Where experts worry is when such groups turn their attention from intelligence gathering to digital sabotage.
questions.solution_en:
The correct order is BCDA.

Sentence B comes first as it provides a platform to carry forward the discussion. It states that all countries use hackers to gather intelligence. C follows B as it gives some instances. So, BC is a pair. Sentence D follows the pair BC and states that the problem arises when countries use their powers in digital wars. The remaining sentence A is the last part of the sentence as it states that the introduction of a device that could potentially be used on an opposing country escalated tensions between two major powerful countries.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully.

She couldn't resist the tempting bargain, a beautiful dress at half the price, (make her day) brighter and her wallet happier.
questions.solution_en:
In this sentence, the phrase "make her day brighter" should be in the present participle form to describe the concurrent action with the main clause. Option (b) is the correct choice. It uses the present participle "making," which fits the context and describes the concurrent action of the beautiful dress making her day brighter.

The rest of the options are grammatically incorrect.

'Is' needs to be followed by either past participle (V3) or present participle (-ing form of the verb), but 'make' is a base verb.

'Had' needs to be followed by the past participle (V3), but 'making' is the -ing form of the verb.

'Was made' [action directed towards the subject which isn't the correct case] fails to make the sentence meaningful.

The corrected sentence: She couldn't resist the tempting bargain, a beautiful dress at half the price, making her day brighter and her wallet happier.

Note:

A participle is a verbal, or a word based off of a verb that expresses a state of being, ending in -ing (present tense) or -ed, -en, -d, -t, -n, or -ne (past tense) that functions as an adjective. This means it needs to modify (or describe) a noun or a pronoun.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

We shall _______ from doing evil.
questions.solution_en:
'Refine' means to purify.

'Refrain' means to stop oneself from doing something.

'Restrain' means to prevent someone from doing something

'Reserve' means to retain for future use.

'Refine' and 'reserve' are not suitable for this context as we cannot purify doing evil and also we cannot retain doing evil for future use.

Among 'refrain' and 'restrain', 'refrain' is more suitable for the context.

We shall refrain from doing evil. This means that we should stop ourselves from doing evil.

We shall restrain from doing evil is incorrect. The correct form is: we shall restrain others from doing evil. This is to restrain to stop someone else from doing something, so 'restrain' should be followed by an object.

B is the right answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank(s).

After eating the ______ pizza, he realized there was a ___ in the box.
questions.solution_en:
The word that fits the first blank is 'whole' because it denotes the quantity that was eaten and the second blank requires a noun that denotes something that is present in the box, once the pizza is eaten, and the suitable word is 'hole'. Accordingly, the option that has the correct order of the words is (a).

Whole- all of; entire.

Hole- a hollow place in a solid body or surface.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).
